proof.criterion: The pull request merges again, by a forward merge of the base rather than a rebase, with nothing of this branch dropped in the resolution.
proof.surface: GitHub's own mergeability for PR #2085, and the seven files the merge conflicted in: plugins.go, plugins_test.go, launcher.go, live_test.go, controller_test.go, docs/kubernetes.md, scripts/e2e/README.md.
proof.command: jj new legion/INFRA-31 main@origin -m 'merge: resolve conflict against main@origin'; resolve; jj git push --bookmark legion/INFRA-31; gh api repos/sjawhar/legion/pulls/2085 --jq '{mergeable, mergeable_state, head: .head.sha}'
proof.observed: Before: `mergeable: false`, `mergeable_state: dirty`. After: `{"head":"f714cec148b6b8175f6b1e128a705e54bd00487e","mergeable":true,"mergeable_state":"blocked"}` — blocked being the review gate, not a conflict. The merge is a genuine fast-forward from both parents, so nothing existing was rewritten.
proof.negativeControl: The pre-merge read is the control, taken twice ten seconds apart by the reviewer and once by me: dirty both times, so the conflict was a settled computation rather than one in flight.

proof.criterion: The lock's two kinds of assertion still pair as they did before the merge, so the base's restructure did not quietly weaken them.
proof.surface: TestTheInstallLockWaitIsABoundInProportionToTheRegistrationDeadline and TestTwoRenderedInstallsSerialiseOnTheSharedBunCache, at the merged head, under the same two mutations the reviewer ran before it.
proof.command: installLockWait's body replaced by `return 1`, then the divisor moved to 4, each `go test -count=1 -run 'TestTheInstallLockWaitIsABound|TestTwoRenderedInstallsSerialise' ./internal/runtime/sandbox/`, restored between
proof.observed: `return 1`: three cases red twice each — `the wait at boot 2m0s x 3 intervals is 1s, want 120s: the 6m0s deadline's third, floored at a second` and `less than the 5s the queue this lock creates needs: the last of a pod's six roles waits for the 5 installs before it`. Divisor 4: the same three cases red once each, on the hand arithmetic alone (`90s, want 120s`; `45s, want 60s`; `60s, want 80s`), the queue clause silent in every one. Restored: `ok … 1.223s`.
proof.negativeControl: The divisor-4 run is the control for the queue clause: silent there and firing under `return 1` is what shows that clause reads the feature rather than the derivation, and it behaves identically either side of the merge.

proof.criterion: The resolution is the union of both sides, not either side wholesale.
proof.surface: The merged plugins.go, plugins_test.go and docs/kubernetes.md read against both parents.
proof.command: go build ./... && go vet -tags e2e ./... && go test -count=1 ./internal/runtime/sandbox/ ./internal/capabilities/... ./internal/config/ ./cmd/legion/ ; bunx biome check . ; bash .github/scripts/check-private-names.sh
proof.observed: All green: sandbox 134.241s, capabilities 25.865s, config 0.733s, cmd/legion 68.166s, gofmt clean, vet ok, biome exit 0, private-names clean. The base's startScript/startArgv/setupBlock and its four setup-command tests are present; so are this branch's --backend=copyfile, the cache read with no default, the flock function with its bounded wait and retry, installLockWait with its whole rationale, requireFlock, the pinned BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR, the serialisation test with its lockless control and the wait's property with its four hand-computed cases. In the documentation both sides' sentences stand, including this branch's floor exception and its five-installs claim scoped above the floor.
proof.negativeControl: The fingerprint is the control and it reports changed, which is the honest answer: the base restructured the code this branch changed, so the branch's diff against its new fork point is a different diff. A resolution that had dropped a correction would have produced the same verdict, so the verdict is not the evidence — the mutations and the suite above are.

filesChanged: Merge commit f714cec148b6 resolves seven conflicted files against main@origin (#2070, the deployment setup command).

packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/plugins.go — this branch's lock, copyfile flag, cache read and installLockWait re-expressed inside the base's installBlock/startScript/startArgv, with the wait threaded as a parameter; both doc comments merged rather than one chosen.
packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/plugins_test.go — both sides' tests, the base's setup-command four and this branch's five, with every assertion of this branch's kept.
packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/launcher.go — the base's startArgv call with this branch's installLockWait argument.
live_test.go, controller_test.go — both sides' option fields.
trickyParts: The base's commit restructured exactly this branch's code, so the merge was structural rather than textual: installScript ceased to exist and its body became installBlock inside a subshell. The lock had to be re-expressed in that shape rather than re-applied as a patch.

A changed fingerprint was unavoidable here and is reported as changed. The rule that a changed fingerprint means a new round rather than a continuation is the reviewer's to apply; smoothing the resolution to make the number match would have been the defect this branch has spent eight rounds removing.
discoveredComplexity: A mergeable read is perishable: the reviewer's and my own reads were MERGEABLE at 23:24 and dirty by 23:58, because the base moved between them. The behind-count's trend, not the status alone, is what says how long the read stays true.
